title: RFC 10017: OAuth 2.0 for Browser-Based Applications
publisher: Internet Engineering Task Force / RFC Editor
summary: Compares browser-only OAuth clients, token-mediating backends, and backend-for-frontend architectures through their different token-custody and session boundaries. Separates protection of token material from the residual authority of compromised same-origin application code.
defensive_use: Document which component holds each credential, binds the user session, and enforces request destinations. Compare those responsibilities and residual risks against an owned application’s architecture.
prerequisites: Browser origins, cookies, and HTTP redirects

access.note: Official specification readable without an account at review time.

published.note: Publication date of this RFC or final specification.

freshness.note: Reviewed this identified edition and its relevant design and security sections. Retrieval date is separate from publication; later revisions or errata may exist.

sources.title: RFC 10017: OAuth 2.0 for Browser-Based Applications

caveats: Backend token custody does not make compromised application code harmless.
Browser-specific guidance complements RFC 9700; it does not establish security of a particular deployment.
